answer: Histories are stored in quill, checked in bridge, and kernel reveals each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 1 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases as the record follows the key, which means laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 690 identities would post 2235 proofs and burn roughly 83 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
